questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What happens if you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effect.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The two together can increase the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The two together can increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and medicine can increase how much they affect your body. For example, one drink mixed with cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on driving. Any extra task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning how to use the vehicle's controls and equipment before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning how to use the vehicle's controls and equipment before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tire tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when a vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speed also increases the risk.

questions.question: If your wheels slip off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the pavement.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: Keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently braking. When safe, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force the vehicle back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves only to the right.
The road turns sharply to the right.
The road curves to the right, then to the left.
The road curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers about hazards ahead. It warns that the road curves right and then left.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:

options.text: Vehicles already in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive with extra care through this area.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and move your vehicle to clear the path. Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals help other drivers know what you plan to do and prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. You can proceed, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
There is a stop sign at the crossing.
Flashing red lights and gates are present and operating.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Avoid road rage by letting it go and continuing to drive safely.

questions.question: Before starting your car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same. This is part of a safe driving routine.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill or curve, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road with a median.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
Road work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you that construction work is coming. Slow down and drive carefully through the work area.

questions.question: You are in an accident. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In an accident, stop right away. Move your car out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with pressure, but do not move injured people. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when:

options.text: Only the driver wears one.
Passengers wear them on long drives.
Everyone wears them on expressways.
Everyone wears them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone wears them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object that can hurt others.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can make you hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and watch for hazards. Keep your eyes moving and do not stare at one spot for too long. This helps you avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because it can cause other drivers to make risky moves.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass before the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and go back to your missed exit.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and go back to your missed exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other cars.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are hardest to see at night compared to signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label on cold and allergy medicine. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medicine.
